title: Neocloud Stocks Sink on Gartner's 80% Failure Warning

tickers.name: Nebius Group N.V. Class A Ordinary Shares
CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Equity markets punished AI infrastructure providers on Thursday, extending a selloff that hit several niche cloud operators. IREN shares fell 8% and NBIS declined 5%, with the latter having suffered a 10% drawdown on Wednesday. CRWV also lost 2.3% on the session. The losses follow research identifying the neocloud segment as the most exposed to a widening gap between capital expenditures and actual revenue.

Gartner predicts that 80% of neocloud providers will cease independent operations by 2030. According to analyst Will Sommer, data center owners need $8.5 trillion in revenue by 2030 to cover spending and a 12% return on invested capital, but will likely generate only $3.6 trillion. This shortfall puts between $3.5 trillion and $4 trillion in asset value at risk of impairment or write-downs through 2032.

selectedTweets.text:
Gartner expects 80% of neocloud providers to cease independent operations by 2030. 

“In 2026, AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure, and are forecast to invest an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030,” said Will Sommer, Sr Director Analyst at Gartner. “However, our research indicates that enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during this period.”

“Through 2030, AI data center owners would need to generate a cumulative $8.5 trillion in revenue to cover announced capital spending, financing costs, and a 12% return on invested capital (ROIC), which we assume to be the hurdle rate of investment capital,” said Sommer. 

“However, total enterprise and consumer AI revenue that can be attributed to AI data centers during this period is forecast to reach no more than $3.6 trillion. Because most AI-native providers operate asset-light business models, we predict that less than half of AI revenue will be earned by providers that own significant AI infrastructure.”

Failure to achieve sustainable ROIC on rapidly depreciating assets would almost certainly necessitate write-downs. Based on Gartner projections, a continued AI infrastructure investment trajectory could leave more than $4 trillion in asset value exposed to write-down risk through 2032. In this scenario, Gartner does not expect the 12% ROIC to be achieved until the end of 2032 at earliest.
